idiom_name: ES module exporting stateless functions (collaborators as arguments or through a factory)
implementation_notes: The classic service class adds nothing in JavaScript: export the domain operation as a named function from a domain/services module and pass collaborators explicitly or close over them in a factory. The module replaces the role structure entirely - there is no instance state to leak and no this to bind - while a frozen object literal or a class of methods is the choice when several operations share one dependency set. Async operations simply return promises, and the caller (the application layer) owns the transaction, the request context and the DTO mapping.
pitfalls: Closures are hidden state: a factory that closes over a mutable variable - a cache, the current request - recreates the stateful service the pattern forbids.
A method passed as a callback loses its this binding; module functions or explicit binding avoid the whole class of bug.
Nothing in the language keeps DTOs out of the interface: document and test that parameters and results are domain objects, not HTTP payloads or database rows.
